items.title: Show HN: A map of outdoor gyms and pull-up bars (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: I've been training mostly outside for over a decade. I spent a decent amount of time in front of a screen, so it's usually a good opportunity to get some sun and fresh air. I used https://calisthenics-parks.com/ for most of that time, but it was always slow and clunky. And then they took the site offline. So, I built this: a map of 25k+ outdoor gyms, pull-up bars, and other exercise stations all over the world. Maybe that's helpful to others. items.title: Ask HN: How do people self host email and maintain deliverability? (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: I wanted to self host my email and decided to rent a VPS. I made sure the ipv4 address was on no blacklist. My domain uses a good TLD with a long domain history. I set up SPF, DKIM, DMARC, reverse IP DNS, etc. I sent 3 emails to my personal outlook/hotmail accounts, all of which went to spam. 1 day later, my IP was banned. Outlook support said they cannot discuss the reason for the ban and will not unban it so I'm out of luck. I know I can just pay a provider $5/month and get email, but there is something about having full control over your own email. Is there anything much I can do? Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50218062 Points: 1 # Comments: 1

items.title: Show HN: Corgi, a helpful {agent, terminal} multiplexer (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: Hey everyone, Inspired by Herdr, I've built an agent multiplexer that I've been using as my daily driver for a few weeks now. I think I improved on the concept in a few ways, focusing on the ergonomics I always wished I had: I show you what the agents are up to, along with a running feed of their activity. There's also a simple shortcut (F1) to go to the next unread agent. I use multiple accounts, so I've added unified launcher for Codex/Claude Code/Pi. Theres some careful ergonomics there: fast search and resume over sessions, inline usage tracking etc. Many small quality of life improvements to the terminal experience: - Links can be copied with a click, so no need to drag-select over many lines - cmd+v just pastes images (even on SSH) - images have a thumbnail preview. - Built-in CPU/Memory/GPU usage tracking, broken down by workspace I assume you have access to cheap inference (Luna/Haiku/etc). It just reuses the agents to organize things for you: what is this http link? what is this worktree about? what is each agent doing? It's small but it made my environment feel more cozy. On a personal note, I've been on a frustrating sick leave for a while now. I created Corgi to challenge myself, and see if I can go back. The answer is more mixed than I had hoped, but I am happy with the result and thankful for the experience. I hope you like it! a few friends & myself have been using it for a few weeks and it's been pretty nice. There's still a lot to improve and some rough edges, so feedback would be greatly appreciated. Thank you :) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50214373 Points: 49 # Comments: 9

items.title: Show HN: Swurf - Swipe through the real web (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: Hello HN, Swurf allows you to swipe through the real web one page after another. It learns what you like and doesn't show you the same page twice. The idea came naturally: there's a seemingly infinite amount of high quality blog posts, random topic rabbit holes, and trending or cool sites that exist which the average person simply will never load on their browser. Swurf solves that by allowing you to rapidly traverse a constantly growing and learning feed of sites that it thinks you'd want to view. Quickly sift through endless pages and find things you like - effortlessly. One of the core drivers for making this project was the desire for real content. The project started as a simple tool for myself to find new and interesting things to learn and read about. Hours spent scrolling on my phone - while it still has its place - is increasingly losing its sense of reward. It's genuinely hard to put into words exactly how swurfin' feels but it's almost refreshing in a sense. I encourage you to try it out and provide feedback. At this time there are no accounts and you can jump in and start swurfin' immediately. There is a three dot menu button on the bottom right which allows you to submit links, save links, control adult content, and search similar topics. One of the things that's great about Swurf is that its almost like a group browsing session (though entirely private) where everyone else who is spending time hunting down great reads or solid sites is helping massage the feed for you and you for them - all within your own set of interests. Enjoy and please ask any questions you have as theres plenty of room to grow. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50205320 Points: 63 # Comments: 29

items.title: Show HN: Impossible Machines: declaratively program the physical world (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: Hey all - Sharing a thought experiment I put together. The premise: what might declarative programming feel like for the physical world? We're already familiar with this paradigm in software land (eg SQL etc where we declare what we want and the execution engine figures out how). I didn't have access to an actuator so I mocked up the concept in software. The way it works is you demonstrate the effect and the system figures out how to achieve it. So say you want to ring a bell and you have a crank. The system will find a way to connect the two. If you add obstacles it figures out how to work around them (runs a constraint solver runs behind the scenes). I think what's interesting about this is being able to think about the problem at a higher level of abstraction, with the system figuring out a way to achieve the intended effect. Anyways, curious to read reactions, feedback, and interesting ideas on how to extend this! Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50202746 Points: 71 # Comments: 17
